chain.label: Promech culture and peer/schedule pressure endorsing weather risk
chain.trigger: Promech's company culture, which tacitly endorsed flying in hazardous weather and failed to manage the risks associated with the competitive pressures affecting Ketchikan-area air tour operators; its lack of a formal safety program

chain.label: Inadequate operational control of the flight release
chain.trigger: Although Promech's General Operations Manual specified that both the pilot and the flight scheduler must jointly agree that a flight can be conducted safely before it is launched, no such explicit concurrence occurred

caused_by.evidence: Promech's training and supervision of the flight scheduler who was on duty on the day of the accident was insufficient to ensure that she fully understood and was performing her responsibilities

chain.label: Pilot's limited local experience and insufficient CFIT-avoidance training
chain.trigger: the accident pilot, who had less than 2 months' experience flying air tours in Southeast Alaska and had demonstrated difficulty calibrating his own risk tolerance

caused_by.evidence: the BATD ... did not provide a realistic decision-making scenario, and the training was insufficient to counteract the cultural and peer influences that encouraged the pilot to continue flight into deteriorating weather

chain.label: Class B TAWS nuisance alerts led to alerting being inhibited
chain.trigger: The switch controlling the accident airplane's TAWS CWA auditory and flag alerting functions was set to the 'inhibit' position ... frequent nuisance alerts during tour operations prompted them to inhibit the alerts

chain.label: Mountainous tree-covered terrain west of Ella Lake
chain.trigger: the high terrain located west of the lake, which includes two similarly shaped mountains

chain.label: Deteriorating weather with obscured terrain over south Ella Lake
chain.trigger: the accident flight encountered deteriorating weather conditions over the southern half of Ella Lake, and, at the time of the accident, the terrain at the accident site was likely obscured by overcast clouds with visibility restricted in rain and mist

chain.label: Pilot chose the riskier short overland route
chain.trigger: he chose to fly the short route despite the presence of low clouds and obscured terrain

caused_by.evidence: the pilot's decision to fly a riskier, overland route despite marginal weather conditions and the availability of a safer, overwater route was influenced by schedule pressure and his attempt to emulate the behavior of other, more experienced pilots whose flights he was following
As a result, the decision to initiate the accident tour rested solely with the accident pilot
had demonstrated difficulty calibrating his own risk tolerance for conducting tour flights in weather that was marginal or below FAA minimums
the route presented an increased risk of an inadvertent encounter with IMC and increased the risk of CFIT

chain.label: Flight conducted at lower-than-normal altitude beneath the clouds
chain.trigger: the accident pilot was flying the route at a relatively low altitude because of the poor weather conditions, which resulted in his viewing terrain from a lower-than-normal vantage point

caused_by.evidence: flying the route at a relatively low altitude because of the poor weather conditions
The accident pilot had transited the area earlier that day about 2,000 ft msl, and other Promech pilots had flown about 2,500 to 3,000 ft msl

chain.label: Continued VFR flight into IMC instead of executing the escape maneuver
chain.trigger: the pilot continued the flight into near-zero visibility conditions ... rather than escape them

caused_by.evidence: the pilot's decision to continue visual flight into an area of instrument meteorological conditions
and then continued the flight into deteriorating weather rather than escape it
the accident pilot experienced difficulty performing the CFIT-avoidance maneuver and, instead of making a level 180° turn as expected, ... made a descending 270° turn

chain.label: Failure to identify navigation landmarks; mistook first mountain for second
chain.trigger: it is possible that the accident pilot mistook the first mountain for the second one and turned the airplane west too early

caused_by.evidence: Visibility was degraded over the south end of Ella Lake; thus, the pilot may not have been able to clearly distinguish some of the landmarks by which he typically navigated
which resulted in his viewing terrain from a lower-than-normal vantage point
his cognitive map of the terrain between Rudyerd Bay and Ketchikan may not have been as detailed or accurate compared to those of other pilots

chain.label: Geographic disorientation and early turn west off the standard route
chain.trigger: the pilot instead deviated from that route and turned the airplane west early (after it passed only the first of the two mountains)

caused_by.evidence: resulted in a navigational error due to geographic disorientation
which resulted in his geographic disorientation and controlled flight into terrain

chain.label: Airplane placed on collision course with 1,900-ft mountain, unwarned
chain.trigger: The pilot's route deviation placed the airplane on a collision course with a 1,900-ft mountain ... the airplane continued on a nearly straight and level flightpath toward the higher terrain for about 30 seconds

caused_by.evidence: the pilot subsequently continued the flight straight and level at an altitude that would have been sufficient to clear terrain on the typical route (but was insufficient to clear the high terrain he was flying toward)
This route allows the flights to avoid the high terrain located west of the lake
the nuisance alerts and associated increase in the use of the inhibit mode prevents the system from effectively providing the intended protection

chain.label: Collision with mountainous, tree-covered terrain
chain.trigger: collided with mountainous, tree-covered terrain about 24 miles east-northeast of Ketchikan ... struck the terrain at an elevation of about 1,600 ft msl

caused_by.evidence: as soon as he realized that the flight was on a collision course with the terrain, he pulled aggressively on the elevator flight controls in an ineffective attempt to avoid the terrain

chain.label: Pilot and eight passengers fatally injured; airplane destroyed
chain.trigger: The commercial pilot and eight passengers sustained fatal injuries, and the airplane was destroyed

caused_by.evidence: based on the damage and high loads sustained during the impact sequence, the accident was not survivable
